english.standardoffencewording:

english.notes:
(i) See H2081 for the wording of the full offence, but note that the attempted offence does not include the element of of recklessness.
(ii) See offence wording: H2082 - where the damage involved is less than five thousand pounds in value .
(iii) Property damaged/destroyed must not belong to defendant(s).
(iv) Consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions is required where damage is to spouse's property (section 30(4) of the Theft Act 1968).
(v) The same incident may involve separate activities, some causing ordinary damage and some damage by fire (for example, protestors break into a laboratory building, smash laboratory equipment and set fire to some files). In such circumstances they are separate offences and best charged as such (R v Booth 1999).

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Ten years imprisonment.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
